summary.headline: FY26 revenue crossed INR 2,000 crore (up 21.6% to INR 2,080 crore) with PAT up 52.4% to INR 168 crore; FY27 plans 60 new facilities.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations up 22.6% YoY to INR 564-565 crore, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR 174 crore (30.2% margin, the highest quarterly margin of the year) despite 19 facility openings. Full-year FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 2,080 crore, EBITDA INR 614 crore (28.9% margin) and PAT INR 168 crore (7.9% margin). Same-store sales growth was about 14%, split roughly equally between volume and value. Management guided to FY27 growth at a similar pace to FY26, EBITDA margins stable, 60 new facilities (40 surgical, 20 clinics), and a merger timeline of roughly Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Surgical services
segments.commentary: 67% of group revenue in FY26; about 323,000 surgeries (+14.5% YoY), with cataract about 73% of surgeries (volume +14.3%).

segments.name: Southern region
segments.commentary: INR 1,273 crore revenue in FY26 (+22.6%), 61% of group; 182 facilities across five southern states.

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: INR 341 crore revenue in FY26 (+19%), 16% of group; 47 facilities.

segments.name: North region
segments.commentary: INR 191 crore revenue in FY26 (+20.7%), 9% of group; 26 facilities. Delhi NCR entered May 2025 and now has several centres.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: About 10.1% of revenue in FY26, with revenue up 20.8% YoY for the full year; 19 facilities.

segments.name: Vintage cohorts FY26
segments.commentary: Pre-FY22 facilities INR 1,375 crore (+14% SSSG, 66% of revenue); FY23 cohort INR 257 crore (+14%); FY24 cohort INR 170 crore (+16%); FY25 cohort INR 223 crore (+72%); FY26 cohort INR 49 crore.

guidance_outlook: Growth in FY27 expected to sustain at a similar pace to FY26, driven by micro-market penetration, new geographies and premium procedures.
EBITDA margins expected to stay stable in FY27 while greenfield expansion continues.
FY27 capex of INR 380-400 crore, including the new Chennai CMS facility.
FY27 acquisition-related deferred payments of about INR 60-65 crore; FY28-30 payments together about INR 60 crore.
Merger of Dr. Agarwal's Healthcare and Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital: shareholder/creditor meetings on July 2, 2026; NCLT sanction expected to conclude in about 5-6 months, i.e. by Q3 FY27.
Chennai CMS facility launch targeted by October 1, 2026, subject to approvals; 12-18 months needed to stabilise.
capex_capacity: FY26 surgery mix: 30 surgical centres opened; FY27 plan of 40 surgical centres (+33%) and 20 clinics, 60 in total, split 30 in H1 and 30 in H2.
Regional FY27 additions: South 24, North 16 (highest ever), West about 15; West and North to more than double additions versus FY26.
Eleven new facilities already launched in FY27 to date (including Faridabad, Ludhiana, Bikaner, Kollam, Mulshi, Nellore).
Delhi NCR: 7-8 more centres planned over 12-18 months; 30 letters of intent in hand for properties.
FY26 network: 269 facilities in India plus 19 in Africa; 19 greenfield openings in Q4 and 148 greenfield facilities added since FY23.
demand_pricing: SSSG of about 14% in FY26: volume about 7% (OPD growth about 5.5%, rest from surgical conversions) and value about 7% (premiumisation about 5.5%, price hikes 1-1.5%).
Average cataract revenue per eye is about INR 41,000-45,000; high-end cataract share rose to 26.3% of 62,800 cataract procedures (FY25: 22.5%).
Femto cataract procedures grew 87% YoY to over 5,900; lenticular (SMILE) refractive procedures grew 19%; retinal surgeries over 12,800 (+23%).
Refractive volumes grew more slowly than cataract; management is in talks with insurers for refractive coverage.
Walk-ins rose to about 10,000 patients a day from about 8,000 (+25%).
Payor mix FY26: 62.4% cash, 28.5% insurance/TPA, 9% government; domestic mix 72% cash.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakdown and the acquisition-related cash outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR 380-400 crore including the CMS facility; acquisition payments are about INR 60-65 crore, versus about INR 85 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What losses do new greenfield facilities carry, and will they recur?
qa_highlights.answer: New FY26 branches had unit-level operating losses of about INR 30 crore (FY25 cohort about INR 21 crore). Management expects a similar drag in FY27, with per-branch losses falling from FY27 onwards, mainly in Delhi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in the listed subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-off merger costs of about INR 80 lakh; corporate office rent of about INR 1 crore for the year; about INR 3.3 crore extra Facebook marketing spend. Merger costs are one-off, rent recurs.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY27 facility additions all organic, and how many facilities closed in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All 60 planned centres are organic; partner deals are not in the pipeline. Five eye clinics were closed in FY26, and AEHL's rental outflow for FY27 is about INR 32 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What limits the pace of openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate at the right cost and compliance with state clinical licences, which can delay openings. Management will ramp up only if the new centres perform.

risks_watch: New-facility drag of about INR 30-40 crore per year could weigh on margins if FY27 openings are weighted to Delhi NCR and the North.
Chennai CMS facility approvals; launch targeted by October 1, 2026, and the timeline already slipped due to election code-of-conduct delays.
Refractive softness relative to cataract; insurance coverage for refractive is still under negotiation.
Paramedical attrition of 21-25% and fixed increments of about 9.5-10%.
Merger completion depends on the July 2, 2026 meetings and final NCLT sanction, expected around Q3 FY27.
Cash-to-insurance mix and the sustainability of about 1.5% price hikes alongside premiumisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and the FY27 pipeline, with specific numbers given readily. Management was more cautious on the timing of approvals (Chennai CMS, merger) and on new-facility losses, and deferred some questions (FY27 new-market count, FY25 subsidiary Q4 cost detail) for later follow-up.
key_quotes: For the first time in our company's history, we crossed over INR 2,000 crores of revenue, a milestone made possible by the trust of over 30 lakh patients and the dedication of every doctor and team member across our network.
On the margin front, we expect our EBITDA margins to stay stable even as we continue to invest aggressively in greenfield expansion, reflecting the underlying operating leverage in our model.
The biggest bottleneck for us, obviously, will be getting the right real estate because one is you want to ensure that you get the right real estate at the right cost.
